value.statement: distant kinsman of the imperial house

sourceUnits.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。
sourceUnits.en: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
sourceUnits.literal: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.

value.event: Sima Ya plotted to restore the heir apparent and carried Sun Xiu's message to Zhang Hua

sourceUnits.zh: 有衛督司馬雅、常從督許超，皆嘗給事東宮，與殿中郎士猗等謀廢賈后，復太子。
sourceUnits.en: Sima Ya, Colonel of the Guards, and Xu Chao, Regular Colonel of the Followers, both former Eastern Palace attendants, joined Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others to plot deposing Empress Jia and restoring the heir apparent.
sourceUnits.literal: The Colonel of the Guards Sima Ya and the Regular Colonel of the Followers Xu Chao, who had both once served the Eastern Palace, joined the Palace Gentleman Shi Yi and others in plotting to depose Empress Jia and restore the Heir Apparent.

sourceUnits.zh: 癸巳，秀使司馬雅告張華曰：「趙王欲與公共匡社稷，為天下除害，使雅以告。」
sourceUnits.en: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join you to save the realm and remove this evil."
sourceUnits.literal: On guisi Xiu had Sima Ya tell Zhang Hua: "The Prince of Zhao wishes to join with you to steady the altars, remove harm for the realm—Ya reports this."

sourceUnits.zh: 雅怒曰：「刃將加頸，猶為是言邪！」
sourceUnits.en: Ya snapped: "The blade is at your neck and you still talk like that!"
sourceUnits.literal: Ya angrily said: "The blade is at the neck—yet you speak thus!"

value.event: Cheng Fu brought the draft for the heir apparent to copy

sourceUnits.zh: 后使黃門侍朗潘岳作書草，令小婢承福，以紙筆及草，因太子醉，稱詔使書之，文曰：「陛下宜自了，不自了，吾當入了之。
sourceUnits.en: The empress had Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Attendant, draft a letter and sent the maid Cheng Fu with paper, brush, and draft. While the heir apparent was drunk she claimed an imperial order and made him copy it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle this yourself. If you do not, I shall enter and settle it.
sourceUnits.literal: The empress had the Yellow Gate Attendant Pan Yue draft a letter, ordered the little maid Cheng Fu to bring paper, brush, and draft; taking advantage of the Heir Apparent's drunkenness she claimed an edict and made him write it. The text read: "Your Majesty ought to settle matters yourself; if you do not settle them, I shall enter and settle them.

sourceUnits.zh: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草，若禱神之文，有如太子素意，因醉而書之，令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之。
sourceUnits.en: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
sourceUnits.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

sourceUnits.zh: '又小婢承福持筆研墨黃紙來，使寫。
sourceUnits.en: Chengfu added brush and yellow paper for the copy.
sourceUnits.literal: Another small maid, Chengfu, brought brush, inkstone, and yellow paper, making him write.

sourceUnits.zh: 有二弟：順、斌。
sourceUnits.en: Two brothers: Shun and Bin.
sourceUnits.literal: Had two younger brothers Shun Bin.

sourceUnits.zh: 弟順、斌
sourceUnits.en: Brothers Shun and Bin.
sourceUnits.literal: Younger brothers Shun Bin.

sourceUnits.zh: 西河繆王斌，字子政，魏中郎。
sourceUnits.en: Sima Bin, Prince Miu of Xihe, styled Zizheng, served Wei as a gentleman of the household.
sourceUnits.literal: Prince Miu of Xihe, Bin, courtesy name Zizheng, was a Gentleman of the Household under Wei.

sourceUnits.zh: 武帝受禪，封陳王，邑千七百一十戶。
sourceUnits.en: Sima Yan made him prince of Chen at 1,710 households.
sourceUnits.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted abdication enfeoffed Prince of Chen one thousand seven hundred ten households.

sourceUnits.zh: 三年，改封西河。
sourceUnits.en: Year three moved the seat to Xihe.
sourceUnits.literal: Third year changed enfeoffment Xihe.

sourceUnits.zh: 咸寧四年薨，子隱立。
sourceUnits.en: In the fourth year of Xianning, Yin inherited.
sourceUnits.literal: In the fourth year of Xianning, Died son Yin succeeded.

value.event: Consort Jiang bore Sima Bin, a son of the crown prince; no calendar date of his birth is stated.

sourceUnits.zh: 太子所幸蔣美人生男，又言宜隆其賞賜，多為皇孫造玩弄之器，太子從之。
sourceUnits.en: When Consort Jiang bore a son they pushed costly toys and stipends—Yu complied.
sourceUnits.literal: When Lady Jiang, whom the crown prince favored, bore a son, they also said rewards should be lavish and many toys fashioned for the imperial grandson; the crown prince obeyed.

sourceUnits.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣為內主。
sourceUnits.en: Heaven blesses our coup—crown Daowen, empower Lady Jiang.
sourceUnits.literal: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.

sourceUnits.zh: 去年十二月，道文疾病困篤，父子之情，實相憐湣。
sourceUnits.en: He mourned son Daowen's fatal illness.
sourceUnits.literal: Last twelfth month Daowen's illness grew desperate—father and son pitied each other truly.

sourceUnits.zh: 自道文病，中宮三遣左右來視，云：'天教呼汝。
sourceUnits.en: Palace runners claimed Heaven summoned Yu.
sourceUnits.literal: Since Daowen fell ill the inner palace thrice sent attendants saying: Heaven summons you.

sourceUnits.zh: 須臾中宮遣陳舞見語：'聞汝表陛下為道文乞王，不得王是成國耳。
sourceUnits.en: They mocked his plea for son's kingship.
sourceUnits.literal: Presently the inner palace sent Chen Wu saying: I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince—you got Cheng principality instead.

sourceUnits.zh: 天與汝酒，當使道文差也。
sourceUnits.en: She tied drinking to son's health.
sourceUnits.literal: Heaven gives you ale so Daowen may recover.

sourceUnits.zh: 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉。
sourceUnits.en: Three sons shared Yu's prison.
sourceUnits.literal: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.

sourceUnits.zh: 虨字道文，永康元年正月，薨。
sourceUnits.en: Eldest Bin (Daowen) died Yongkang first month.
sourceUnits.literal: Bin, courtesy name Daowen, died in the first month of Yongkang year one.

sourceUnits.zh: 四月，追封南陽王。
sourceUnits.en: Fourth month titled Prince of Nanyang.
sourceUnits.literal: In the fourth month posthumous investiture as Prince of Nanyang.

value.event: Cited as a historical exemplar in Meng Da's writing

sourceUnits.zh: 故申生、衛伋、禦寇、楚建禀受形之氣，當嗣立之正，而猶如此。
sourceUnits.en: Shensheng, Ji of Wei, Yu Kou, and Jian of Chu were lawful heirs—yet each met doom.
sourceUnits.literal: Therefore Shensheng, Wei Ji, Yu Kou, and Chu Jian received their bodily qi with rightful claim to succession, yet still came to this.

sourceUnits.zh: 遂使冤逾楚建，酷甚戾園。
sourceUnits.en: Compared Yu's fate to ancient prince tragedies.
sourceUnits.literal: Thereupon wrong exceeded Chu Jian's case; cruelty surpassed Liyuan's prison.

value.event: Jin-era ancestor of Meng Huaiyu.

sourceUnits.zh: 高祖珩，晉河南尹。
sourceUnits.en: Emperor Wu's father Heng had been Jin administrator of Henan.
sourceUnits.literal: The Gaozu's father Heng was Jin Administrator of Henan.

value.event: Xie Jie served as inspector before being killed in AD 300.

sourceUnits.zh: 劾案沛王韜獄，未竟，會解結代楊准為刺史，韜因河間王顒屬結。
sourceUnits.en: He was investigating Prince Pei's man Tao when Xie Jie replaced Yang Zhun as regional inspector; Tao then leaned on Sima Yong, the Prince of Hejian, to bring pressure on Xie Jie.
sourceUnits.literal: He impeached and investigated the case of Prince of Pei's Tao; it was not finished when Xie Jie replaced Yang Zhun as inspector, and Tao through Prince of Hejian Yong importuned Jie.

value.event: Yang Zhun was appointed literary aide at the Guangling enfeoffment; no era or year is stated.

value.event: Pei Quan warned the heir apparent about Jia Mi

sourceUnits.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「謐，后所親暱，一旦交構，則事危矣。」
sourceUnits.en: Steward Pei Quan warned him: "Mi is the empress's favorite. If you quarrel with him, disaster will follow."
sourceUnits.literal: The Steward Pei Quan remonstrated: "Mi is one the empress cherishes; if you should clash, the affair would be perilous."

value.event: Pei Quan warned that Jia Mi's disrespect could ruin the great enterprise; no calendar date is stated.

sourceUnits.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「賈謐甚有寵于中宮，而有不順之色，若一旦交構，大事去矣。
sourceUnits.en: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: "Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.
sourceUnits.literal: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: 'Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.

sourceUnits.zh: 宜深自謙屈，以防其變，廣延賢士，用自輔翼。」
sourceUnits.en: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings."
sourceUnits.literal: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings.'

value.event: Guo Huai urged Empress Jia to cherish the heir apparent and warned her on her deathbed

sourceUnits.zh: 頠旦夕說其從母廣城君，令戒諭賈后以親厚太子，賈模亦數為后言禍福；
sourceUnits.en: Pei pressed his aunt, the Lady of Guangcheng, day and night to warn Empress Jia to treat the heir apparent kindly. Jia Mo likewise urged the empress repeatedly about the risks she was courting;
sourceUnits.literal: Pei day and night urged his mother's younger sister, the Lady of Guangcheng, to admonish Empress Jia to treat the Heir Apparent with affection; Jia Mo also repeatedly spoke to the empress of fortune and calamity;

sourceUnits.zh: 初，廣城君郭槐，以賈后無子，常勸后使慈愛太子。
sourceUnits.en: Earlier Guo Huai, Lady of Guangcheng, because Empress Jia had no son of her own, often urged her to treat the heir apparent kindly.
sourceUnits.literal: Earlier the Lady of Guangcheng, Guo Huai, because Empress Jia had no son, often urged the empress to treat the Heir Apparent with kindness.

sourceUnits.zh: 賈謐驕縱，數無禮於太子，廣城君恆切責之。
sourceUnits.en: Jia Mi was arrogant and repeatedly insulted the heir apparent. The Lady of Guangcheng scolded him harshly again and again.
sourceUnits.literal: Jia Mi was arrogant and unrestrained, repeatedly disrespectful toward the Heir Apparent; the Lady of Guangcheng constantly rebuked him sharply.

sourceUnits.zh: 廣城君欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固；
sourceUnits.en: The Lady of Guangcheng wanted Han Shou's daughter as the heir apparent's consort, and the heir apparent likewise hoped to marry into the Han clan to strengthen his position;
sourceUnits.literal: The Lady of Guangcheng wished to make Han Shou's daughter the Heir Apparent's consort; the Heir Apparent also wished to marry into the Han clan to secure himself;

sourceUnits.zh: 及廣城君病，臨終，執后手，令盡心於太子，言甚切至。
sourceUnits.en: When the Lady of Guangcheng fell mortally ill, she took the empress's hand at the end and urged her with utmost earnestness to devote herself to the heir apparent.
sourceUnits.literal: When the Lady of Guangcheng fell ill, at the end she took the empress's hand and ordered her to devote her heart to the Heir Apparent, her words very earnest.

value.event: Guo Huai wished to make Han Shou's daughter the crown princess; no calendar date is stated.

sourceUnits.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
sourceUnits.en: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.
sourceUnits.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.

value.action: respected the heir Minhuai and urged her daughter to love him; rebuked Jia Mi

value.event: died after a grave illness

sourceUnits.zh: 后母廣城君養孫賈謐干預國事，權侔人主。
sourceUnits.en: Lady Guo raised Jia Mi—his power rivaled the throne.
sourceUnits.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng raised grandson Jia Mi meddling state affairs—authority matched sovereign.

sourceUnits.zh: 后母廣城君以后無子，甚敬重愍懷，每勸厲后，使加慈愛。
sourceUnits.en: Lady Guo prized Minhuai—begged Jia to cherish him.
sourceUnits.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng because consort lacked sons greatly revered Crown Prince Minhuai—often urged consort—made her add kindness.

sourceUnits.zh: 賈謐恃貴驕縱，不能推崇太子，廣城君恒切責之。
sourceUnits.en: Jia Mi insulted the heir—Lady Guo scolded him.
sourceUnits.literal: Jia Mi relied on pride—could not honor crown prince—Lady Guangcheng constantly scolded.

sourceUnits.zh: 及廣城君病篤，占術謂不宜封廣城，乃改封宜城。
sourceUnits.en: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—she became Princess Yicheng.
sourceUnits.literal: When Lady Guangcheng gravely ill—divination said unsuitable enfeoff Guangcheng—thereupon changed enfeoff Yicheng.

sourceUnits.zh: 宜城臨終執后手，令盡意于太子，言甚切至。
sourceUnits.en: She clasped Jia’s hand—beg her shield Minhuai.
sourceUnits.literal: Yicheng dying grasped consort’s hand—ordered exhaust feeling toward crown prince—speech extremely earnest.

sourceUnits.zh: 又曰：「趙粲及午必亂汝事，我死後，勿復聽入，深憶吾言。」
sourceUnits.en: She also said, "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely disrupt your affairs; after I die, do not admit them again—remember my words well."
sourceUnits.literal: Also said: “Zhao Can and Wu surely ruin your affairs—after I die—never hear them again—deeply remember my words.”

value.event: Yan Xun wept over Zhang Hua's corpse

sourceUnits.zh: 閻纘撫張華屍慟哭曰：「早語君遜位而不肯，今果不免，命也！」
sourceUnits.en: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I urged you to resign and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"
sourceUnits.literal: Yan Xun stroked Zhang Hua's corpse and wailed: "I told you early to yield your post and you would not; now you could not escape—fate!"

sourceUnits.zh: 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台，故臣江統、陸機並作誄頌焉。
sourceUnits.en: Yan Zuan's plea built Son-Lament Terrace—Jiang Tong and Lu Ji wrote elegies.
sourceUnits.literal: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.

dateContext.event: Killed by Prince Yi on suspicion of divided loyalty.

value.event: Killed in the seventh month of Tai'an 2.

sourceUnits.zh: 二年春正月甲子朔，赦五歲刑。
sourceUnits.en: The new year opened with remission of all penal labor sentences up to five years.
sourceUnits.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, on the jiazi new moon, five-year sentences were amnestied.

sourceUnits.zh: 秋七月，中書令卞粹、侍中馮蓀、河南尹李含等貳於長沙王乂，乂疑而害之。
sourceUnits.en: In the seventh month Prince Yi suspected Bian Cui, Feng Sun, Li Han, and others of divided loyalty and had them killed.
sourceUnits.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Director of the Secretariat Bian Cui, Palace Attendant Feng Sun, Intendant of Henan Li Han, and others were double-minded toward Prince Yi of Changsha; Yi suspected them and harmed them.
